request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [redacted] 
Age: 28 years 
Sex: Female 

Date of Admission: [redacted] 
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Reason for Admission:
The patient presented with right hip pain after a fall and was diagnosed with a pathologic hip fracture. 

Clinical Course:
Following admission, the patient underwent radiographic and imaging studies which revealed lytic lesions in the femoral neck and intertrochanteric region as well as osseous destructive lesions in the lumbar spine. The bone scan was suggestive of metastatic disease. A biopsy revealed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with aggressive features and a germinal center subtype histology. The patient underwent a total right hip replacement and returned for follow-up evaluation.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was managed for the pathologic hip fracture and underwent biopsy that confirmed the diagnosis of lymphoma. Following diagnosis, the patient underwent a total right hip replacement. The patient is scheduled for further evaluation and management by the oncology team. 

Discharge Medications: 
See the oncology team. 

Follow-up Plan: 
The patient is to follow up with the oncology team. 

Discharge Condition: 
The patient is stable.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
In ICD-10-AM, a pathological fracture due to neoplastic disease is coded to M84.5 (pathological fracture in neoplastic disease). That code carries a "code also" note for the underlying neoplasm. The Australian Coding Standards say that when a pathological fracture is due to malignancy, the malignancy is sequenced as the principal diagnosis.

Here, the diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is the underlying cause, and the admission was for managing the fracture, with the lymphoma confirmed by biopsy. Under ICD-10-AM the M84.5 category has an asterisk-style "code first" convention: "Pathological fracture in neoplastic disease" is listed as M84.5* in ICD-10 WHO, where the underlying neoplasm is the dagger. In ICD-10-AM, M84.5 is not an asterisk code, but ACS 0044 (or similar) directs that the neoplasm be coded first when the fracture is caused by it.

The principal diagnosis is therefore the lymphoma. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma is coded to C83.3. With bone involvement being secondary, it is still C83.3.

CODE: C83
